about: The epistola of the formulary “Nativity of the Lord — Mass during the Day” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: God, Who at sundry times and in divers manners spoke in times past to the fathers through the Prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us through His Son, Whom He appointed heir of all things and through Whom He made the ages. He, being the brightness of glory and the figure of His substance, upholdeth all things by the word of His power; having made purification of sins, He sitteth at the right hand of the Majesty on high. He became so much better than the Angels as He inherited a name more excellent than theirs. For unto which of the Angels said He at any time: Thou art My Son; this day have I begotten Thee? And again: I will be to Him a Father, and He shall be to Me a Son? And when He again bringeth the Firstborn into the world, He saith: Let all the Angels of God adore Him. Of the Angels indeed He saith: Who maketh His Angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire. But unto the Son: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever; a scepter of righteousness is the scepter of Thy kingdom. Thou hast loved justice and hated iniquity; therefore God, Thy God, hath anointed Thee with the oil of gladness above Thy fellows. And: Thou in the beginning, O Lord, didst found the earth, and the heavens are the works of Thy hands. They shall perish, but Thou shalt remain; they shall all grow old as a garment. As a mantle Thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed; but Thou art the selfsame, and Thy years shall not fail.
